cover.title: When clouds close in, the lakes stay in view.
cover.lede: Pakistan's glacial lakes fill and burst in summer, when cloud hides them from optical satellites. SARtale uses NASA–ISRO NISAR radar, which sees through cloud. It gives each lake one plain status.

risk.label: 01 · The flood
risk.title: Shisper, 7 May 2022
risk.body: On 7 May 2022 the ice-dammed lake beside Shisper glacier burst. The flood destroyed the Karakoram Highway bridge at Hassanabad. The bridge was 6.6 km from the lake basin in a straight line. The flood cut the road between central and upper Hunza.
risk.source: Sources: Dawn, 7 May 2022 (dawn.com/news/1688466) and 8 May 2022 (dawn.com/news/1688567). The 6.6 km is the straight line from the register point at the lake basin to the bridge (OpenStreetMap way 651792498). It is not the flood's path down the gorge.

shadow.title: Mountains cast shadows too
shadow.lede: Glacial lakes sit in deep, steep valleys. Shadow can hide a lake from both kinds of satellite, and a dark shadow can be mistaken for water.

cards.label: Optical satellites
cards.text: The sun's shadow falls across slopes and valley floors. A shaded lake can be missed, and a shaded slope can look like water.

cards.label: Radar
cards.text: Radar looks sideways. Slopes facing away from the satellite fall in radar shadow, and steep slopes facing it fold over (layover). Both can hide a shoreline.

cards.label: What SARtale does
cards.text: Shadow and layover fall on the valley walls, almost never on a flat lake. SARtale masks nothing inside a lake's zone. A terrain model maps the walls in radar shadow or layover. SARtale excludes these walls from the window median used to measure water. If less than {minObservable} of a lake's zone can be seen, the status is Not observable.

shadow.sourcesLead: Radar shadow and layover are among the main limits of SAR lake mapping in the Himalaya (

sources.after: ). Comparing ascending and descending passes reduces shadow errors (

sources.text: a 2026 study in Norway, Journal of Glaciology
sources.after: ). Terrain shadow also causes errors in optical lake maps (

measure.label: 04 · The measurement
measure.title: Dark radar pixels become a water area
measure.imageAlt: {attabadName} in NISAR radar on {attabadDate}, with the water SARtale reads shown in blue
measure.waterAlt: Water pixels read from the radar image, shown in blue
measure.caption: {attabadDate}, track {attabadTrack}. Blue: water read from radar, inside the lake outline (OpenStreetMap).
steps: Calm water reflects radar away, so it is dark in HH, the channel that tells water from land best here.
SARtale smooths the speckle. A pixel is water when its HH is at least 3 dB darker than the median of its 6 km window. Terrain in radar shadow or layover is excluded from that median.

SARtale counts water inside the lake's zone. It compares each pass with the median of earlier passes on its own track. One pass beyond twice the noise is a Watch. Two passes in a row with growth beyond twice the noise give an Alert.

watch.label: 05 · The levels
watch.title: {sites} sites, one plain status each
watch.lede: Latest pass {latest}. Each status compares a lake with its own earlier passes and its own noise. Levels are No change, Watch, Alert: growing or Decrease noted. A site with no lake now stays on the list to monitor whether a lake forms.

add.label: 06 · Add a lake
add.title: Know a lake we are not watching?
add.body: Give the lake a name. Enter its coordinates. State where they come from. SARtale searches NASA's catalogue for NISAR passes over the lake and reads a 6 km window from each. It gives a level once a track has {minLooks} earlier passes to compare with a new pass.
steps: Requested: the request opens as a GitHub issue.
Searched: NISAR passes over the point are counted.
Watched: after the team accepts it, a level appears once a track has {minLooks} earlier passes.
